name: cloud-me
description: Diego's Cloud Me — the personal-administration half of the constellation. Where Cloud SuperApp is the launcher for everything the cloud runs, Cloud Me is the launcher for everything the PERSON runs: paperwork and money (Buro), what is due (Agenda), the public profile (Me), travel and health (Projects) and study (Studying). It stores almost nothing of its own — cards live in Cloud Wallet, passwords in Cloud Vault, files in cloud-myterminal, health records in Health Connect — and is the one screen that indexes all of them.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-Wallet, cloud-myterminal, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Bump here, rebuild devShell.

_doc_modules: Every libs:* entry is shared BY REFERENCE (`dir`) out of ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs — Cloud Me owns no library source of its own. That is the whole design: the app is an assembly. libs:health draws MyHealth, libs:fin draws the accounting dashboard. The calendar is the one exception: Agenda's events and todos come from the cal ENGINE (Cloud-Lib-Cal.apk), bound over IPC through build.json::engines.cal, not compiled in. A fix in any of them lands here on the next build with no copy to keep in step.

libs:databackend._doc_dir: #825 the engine wire (IDataBackend + DataBackendClient/Service), out of libs:core so a wire edit rebuilds only the engines and the apps that bind one.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

engines._doc: ENGINES THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING (engine-apk-split, move 3; same shape as ac_cloud-drive/build.json::engines). Each is a Cloud-Lib-*.apk the Store installs (a fleet row of kind lib) whose service answers core's IDataBackend; this app links nothing of the engine's module, so an engine change republishes that one APK and not this app. `fleet` is the Store row in aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json from which app/build.gradle resolves the package (an id the manifest lacks fails the build); `action` finds the service in that package ({package} substituted at build time, matching the engine manifest's ${applicationId}.ENGINE); `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT that answers every method this app calls, read through PackageManager BEFORE binding so an engine too old for this build is named as such. The engine keeps its own cache: Agenda here and Cloud Tasks share one synced calendar and one task mirror.

ui._doc: Cloud Me's whole navigation is this block: seven bottom-nav sections (`ui.bottom_nav`, in order: Health, Study, Achieves, Profile, Duties, Buro, LLC), the Settings entries at the top right (`ui.settings`: the sections the top bar's Profile and Configs icons open; the left side menu opens by tapping the hamburger only, there is no swipe gesture), and the page tabs of every section drawn as Samsung-Health icon pills (icon-only, the selected tab also shows its name). A section's `pages` are its tab strip, and a page may declare `pages` of its own. A page with an `action` is a launch tab: it hands that `extapp:`/`page:` target to MainActivity.onTarget instead of showing content (Buro > Account launches Cloud Account). Page CONTENT is not here: each page is a file at data/ui/<section>/<page>.json, shipped as an asset. The same `page:<section>/<page>` grammar arrives from OUTSIDE the app too: the SuperApp's Dashboard icons launch Cloud Me with a `shortcut_action` extra carrying one of these strings.

permissions._doc: Configs > Perms, declared: EVERY permission Cloud Me needs. `entries` are ids of the shared libs:perms catalogue (ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/perms/src/main/assets/perms-catalogue.json), which owns each one's label, kind (runtime dialog, special settings page, app-op, OEM guide), live check and settings intents; `why` is Cloud Me's reason, one line on the row; `icon` is a libs:ui-icons name; `used: false` marks a permission on the list that no feature uses yet, shown collapsed under Not used yet (still in Grant all). `install` are install-time permissions, listed as granted. `health` is the Health Connect set: `read` is the SuperApp's exact set (libs:health's manifest), `write` what Health > Tracked's manual entry writes. MePerms.kt holds no permission name. The start-up rule (MePermPlan.startup): runtime permissions never asked are asked, a denied one is asked again until Android stops showing its dialog (permanently denied: never again at start), Health Connect is asked until it has been declined twice (Health Connect's own limit), a special access is opened once on first launch and then only from the banner or Grant all. test/test-me-perms.sh pins this list to AndroidManifest.xml both ways.

entries.why: Update progress and the updater's notices.
Agenda reads your CalDAV events and todos.
Steps and active minutes without a watch.
Heart rate from a connected wearable.
Installs new Cloud Me builds from GHCR.
Agenda and Duties reminders, once they exist.
Documents in shared storage, once a page needs it.
Screen time for Circadian and Sleep, once they read it.
Reading notifications, once a listener ships.
Drawing over other apps, once a screen needs it.
Keeps updates, prefetch and Health sync out of Doze.
The same background work on One UI.
Stops Samsung's battery manager pausing sync.

health.rationale: Cloud Me reads your activity, heart, sleep, body, nutrition and cycle records from Health Connect to draw the Health section, and writes only the entries you add by hand on Health > Tracked (steps, distance, active calories, workouts, heart rate, sleep, weight, water). Nothing leaves the phone: Health Connect data is never uploaded.

ui._doc_external_apps: Resolves an `extapp:<id>` target to a package to launch. Cloud Me links out far more than it stores, so this table is load-bearing: a tile whose id is missing here is skipped rather than crashing, which is also how an app you have not installed simply does not appear.

sections._doc: Health — a bar section of its own (it was a shortcut into Projects > Health). Two page groups (Plan: index, 12 plan pages and the workout plan; Trackers: Tracked, the Google Fit / Samsung Health style today dashboard over Health Connect, and 4 more) on the many_rows nav mode, the groups referencing the flat pages list by id. Every page is drawn by the app's own Compose HealthPage from data/health/*.json (the declared plan, formulas and workout) and the user's entries (SharedPreferences health_user, a declared fleet-config store); the trackers read Health Connect live and say so when it is empty. The metric taxonomy stays here because libs:health's build.gradle looks it up by SECTION ID (`ui.sections[id=health].metrics`).
sections._doc_metrics: Data-driven metric taxonomy — read by SummaryPage / TimelinePage / ConfigsPage to render the per-metric tiles + drill-downs. Each metric maps to one-or-more Health Connect record types via `records` (matched at runtime by class simple-name) + the perm subset via `perm_keys`. Add a metric = one entry here + tile icon. Removing a metric here removes it from all 3 top-level pages.
sections.label: Health

sections._doc: Experiences (#1350): Study and Achieves merged into one section with three subpages. Work is a Done and To do ledger over experiences_user (work_done / work_todo), its Done list seeded by data/regen-study.py with the LinkedIn roles (the same source as LLC > Employed). Study keeps CV and Roadmap (data/regen-study.py). Personal Achieves holds the Achieves tabs: each tab is one kind of experience, holding a Done and a To do list of the owner's own records (add, edit, mark done with today's date, mark undone), all in the declared config store experiences_user so the backup and the new-phone migration carry them. Geo is first: every place visited with live stats (cities, countries, continents, % of world, grouped by continent and country, first and last visit) and a wishlist; the International Experience text and the old Trips tools moved into it. Endurance holds Travel & Adventure (the old Experiences rows and the Personal Pursuits text), Personal Growth holds Personal Growth, Health & Wellness, Creativity & Fun and Career and Finance (with the B1 Personal text), Community holds Relationship & Community, By 30 / By 40 / By 50 hold the Bucket 50 age goals. ui.sections[achieves].migration moves the old done/todo records into the matching tab on first load; LegacyRoutes sends the old page ids to their new tab. Every page id is unique in the section, so page:experiences/<id> reaches any of them; LegacyRoutes maps the old study and achieves routes here.

migration._doc: Achieves migration (store experiences_user): the old Experiences page kept its records in the collections done and todo. On load, each record moves to <tab>_done or <tab>_todo by its category; a category this map does not name goes to the default tab, so nothing is dropped. The old collections are then removed, which makes the migration run once.

sections.label: Experiences

sections._doc: Lnktree (#1299: formerly Profile, section id `me`; LegacyRoutes keeps `me` as an alias so old deep links, shortcuts and saved state still open it) — the app's namesake and its centre slot, in two halves: Professional is the LinkedIn profile, Personal is the Instagram one. Both are generated by data/regen-profile.py from the same files the web pages hydrate from, so neither is prose typed twice. The switcher is the section's ordinary tab strip. The app OPENS here — `ui.default_section`. The app opens here (`ui.default_section` = lnktree). Tasks moved out to Duties. Two rows (horizontal_two_rows groups, `separator_before` draws the "|" inside a row): Prof = Professional | Leaf.y, Nexus.z, Stark.x; Pers = Personal, Social | Health, DD, Astro | Lnktree. Leaf.y, Nexus.z, Stark.x, Astro and Lnktree are published sites embedded by https URL (data/ui/lnktree/<id>.json). #1298 a third row Proj (below Pers): its chips are the registry AREAS (ui.repo_tree.areas: the registry areas flagged show_in lnktree in repos-github.json areas[]; labels read from the outline), each page the repo tree of that area; tapping the Proj label opens the whole outline with Expand all / Collapse all. The tree is data, never typed here: libs:repos repos.outline.json, shipped byte-equal as data/repos/repos.outline.json.
sections.label: Lnktree

sections._doc: Configs — reached from the gear at the top right rather than the drawer, because it is the one destination you want from wherever you are. ONE page, no tab strip: a settings screen is a list you scroll, which is how every other app in the constellation lays its Configs out. Permissions first, then About with the version, the commit and the self-update control, then the way out to the rest of the constellation.
sections.label: Configs

repo_tree._doc: #1298 Lnktree > Proj: the registry outline as a collapsible tree. outline_asset is libs:repos repos.outline.json (byte-equal copy in data/repos, guarded by RepoOutlineTest and libs/repos/sync.sh --check-outline). group is the second-row group whose label opens the FULL tree. areas maps each page of that group to a registry area code, in registry order. NO names here: a chip label, the area order and which areas are listed all come from the registry (git-repos-master projects-repos.json: area name, and the area flag show_in containing lnktree), through the outline; app/build.gradle bakes each chip label from the outline and RepoTreeTest guards that nothing is overridden. Expansion state is the SharedPreferences store repo_tree (one set of expanded node codes, declared in fleet-config.json). A leaf opens the fleet app whose constellation repo_url is its url when there is one, else its GitHub url.

lnktree_cache._doc: #1323 Lnktree page cache. The https pages of `section` (Leaf.y, Nexus.z, Stark.x, Astro, Lnktree) are cached on disk by the app itself (shouldInterceptRequest, files keyed by the URL: the HTML plus its same-origin CSS/JS/images), because the WebView's HTTP cache follows the server's headers, cannot be aged, listed or emptied per page. An entry older than ttl_days is STALE: it is still shown at once and refetched in the background (stale-while-revalidate); offline it is shown as is. Each visited page keeps its WebView alive (LRU of holder_max_webviews), so switching never reloads. Pull-down at the page's top is a HARD refresh: hard_refresh_scope `page` deletes that page's cache files (`all` = every Lnktree cache file), empties the WebView cache and reloads from the network. prefetch: at app start, in the background (WorkManager, never blocks start-up), every page with no valid entry is downloaded with its subresources: concurrency pages at a time, network `unmetered` or `connected`, at most max_pages pages and max_subresources_per_page files each. max_cache_mb trims the oldest entries. exclude_pages lists page ids that opt out. An absent block turns it all off.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Me as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-me-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-me-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh; the ship workflow calls it. Until 2026-09-10 no workflow called ANY tester for this application, so test-ui-pages.sh sat in the tree unexecuted and the ship run's only question was whether Gradle exited 0.

shell._doc_requires: Tools a tester shells out to. A missing tool must be LOUD AND FATAL: a tester whose command is not found produces a verdict from the tool's ABSENCE, which reads as a pass. Both testers here read build.json with python3 and nothing else.

unit._doc: Robolectric suite under app/src/test/ (#531): MeBottomNavTest inflates the REAL activity_main under Theme.CloudMe, configures the bottom-nav island exactly as MainActivity does (MeBottomNav.configure) and measures it - bar order, pill paint, tap routing, clearance, and that the page ends where the island begins.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json). general.sections: the anchors and sections of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs). about: what the app does, its features, privacy and the fleet services it talks to (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time). Name, icon, version, build sha, repo, licence, crash sink and debug API are derived, never typed here.

about.what: The personal-administration hub: health, experiences, roadmap, links, duties, paperwork and the company, for the person rather than the cloud.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.
